title: County health-sector capacity and vehicle constraint occupy four distinct place cells
source_unit: US county; 2023 CBP employer establishment stock joined to 2023 population, 2023 ACS 5-year vehicle/commute/mode/rent/crowding/language/income/vacancy context, 2023 QCEW all-industry wage context, 2023 Census BPS permit flow, HRSA primary-care designation, and USDA RUCC

observations.period: 2023; low health capacity / low zero-vehicle-household share cell

median_long_commute_pct.unit: percent of ACS workers not working from home with 30+ minute commute

median_gross_rent.unit: dollars per month; ACS median gross rent

median_crowded_units_pct.unit: percent of occupied housing units with more than one occupant per room

median_limited_english_pct.unit: percent of population age 5+ in limited-English households

population_weighted_hpsa_share.unit: percent of cell population in counties represented by a designated primary-care HPSA component

population_weighted_nonmetro_share.unit: percent of cell population in RUCC codes 4–9

median_qcew_avg_weekly_wage.unit: US dollars per week; QCEW county all-industry average weekly wage, county median

median_permit_units_per_1000.unit: 2023 Census BPS permitted housing units per 1,000 residents

median_permit_buildings_per_1000.unit: 2023 Census BPS permitted buildings per 1,000 residents

median_public_transit_commute_pct.unit: percent of ACS workers commuting by public transportation

median_walk_commute_pct.unit: percent of ACS workers walking to work

median_worked_from_home_pct.unit: percent of ACS workers working from home

observations.method: County-level descriptive cell summary; health-establishment density and zero-vehicle share split at unweighted county medians; HPSA and RUCC shares population-weighted.
observations.uncertainty: ACS margins of error are not propagated; CBP suppressed employment, provider adequacy, neighboring supply, price, hours, quality, and use remain unmeasured.
observations.subgroup: Counties below the 23.132 health-establishment-per-10,000 median and below the 5.322% zero-vehicle-household median.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low zero-vehicle share can reflect car access or different settlement/transit patterns; it is not a complete mobility-success measure.

related_sources.claim: Current primary-care HPSA designation context joined by county identifier.
2023 RUCC context used for population-weighted nonmetro shares.
2023 QCEW county all-industry average weekly wage context.
2023 annual county building-permit units and buildings context.
ACS means-of-transportation-to-work context for public transit, walking, and work-from-home shares.
Reproduction script and median split/cell definitions.

boundary: A high zero-vehicle share is a mobility constraint context, not a complete measure of mobility options; QCEW average weekly wage is not a median worker wage or household income; BPS permits are not completed or occupied housing; commute mode and work-from-home shares do not establish service destinations, transit quality, trip reliability, or care access; destination, affordability, and travel reliability require separate data.
method: County-level descriptive four-cell comparison; health/social-assistance establishment density and zero-vehicle-household share are split at unweighted county medians in the 3,006-county complete-input frame; cell summaries retain population weights for HPSA and rurality shares; QCEW average weekly wage is an establishment-based county context measure and BPS values are annual permitted units/buildings; ACS mode values summarize commuting population shares.
uncertainty: ACS margins of error are not propagated; QCEW wage disclosure and coverage rules, BPS geographic coverage and permit authorization versus completion, CBP suppressed employment, commute-mode categories, provider adequacy, neighboring supply, prices, hours, quality, use, and causal effects remain unmeasured.
